chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, from one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I have not seen among the weak in religion and deficient in intellect anyone more robbing of the reason of a man of sound mind than you (women).'

key_terms.أَسْلَبَ: Most robbing/captivating — superlative form indicating an exceptional capacity to draw away reason
key_terms.ضَعِيفَاتِ الدِّينِ: Weak ones of religion — referring to legal exemptions from certain religious obligations
key_terms.لُبٍّ: Sound intellect, core reason — contrasted with superficial 'aql; the lubb is the inner kernel of wisdom
key_terms.مِنْكُنَّ: Than you all (feminine plural) — addressing women present at the time
key_terms.نَاقِصَاتِ الْعُقُولِ: Deficient in intellect — contested term; some scholars interpret it as referring to testimonial differences in fiqh

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about women being weak in religion and deficient in intellect in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) relayed through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) concerning women's characterization as weak in faith and deficient in intellect, yet able to captivate men of sound reason. Classical Shia scholarship interprets 'weakness in religion' as a reference to exemptions from certain ritual obligations (prayer during menstruation, fewer testimonial duties), while 'deficiency in intellect' has historically been debated — some scholars viewing it as contextual or referring to a specific group. The saying warns men of sound mind (dhul-lubb) to guard themselves against being led astray through heedlessness of worldly attachments.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al Ja’fary, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> have not seen from the weak ones of the Religion, and the deficient of the intellects, ones with a stiff heart more than you (women)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Sulayman ibn Ja’far al-Ja’fariy from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘I never saw anyone more snatching from an intelligent person, than these weak in religion, deficient of reason; you women are.’”
